items.t: All traffic uses HTTPS with modern TLS
items.d: No plain HTTP anywhere; no disabled certificate validation, even in dev builds.
Session and refresh tokens in secure storage — not AsyncStorage, localStorage or files.
The server checks the user may touch the resource — not just that they're logged in.

items.t: No secrets ship in the app bundle
items.d: Payment, AI/LLM and service keys stay on your server behind an API you control.

items.t: All input is validated on the server
items.d: Client-side checks are UX; the server validates and sanitizes everything regardless.
npm audit / Dependabot (or similar) run in CI; security patches applied promptly.
Login, OTP and password flows are throttled to block credential-stuffing.

items.t: Sessions expire and can be revoked
items.d: Short-lived access tokens with refresh rotation; server-side kill switch for a compromised session.

items.t: Sensitive data is encrypted at rest
items.d: PII and business data encrypted in the database; backups included; access logged.
Crash + security alerting exists, and someone owns the response when it fires.

verdicts.title: Solid:
verdicts.text: Your foundations look strong. Keep dependencies moving, re-run this quarterly, and consider a periodic external review to keep yourselves honest.

verdicts.title: Gaps to close:
verdicts.text: Real gaps, but fixable ones. Prioritise anything you answered "No" on that touches tokens, secrets or server-side authorization — those are the breach-makers. Most fixes take days, not months.

verdicts.title: At risk:
verdicts.text: Treat hardening as this sprint's work, not backlog. Start with transport security, token storage and server-side auth — then work down the list. This is well-understood engineering; you don't need a security team to fix it.
